title: Flexbox
subtitle: 1D layout with flex container and items
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: Before Flexbox, centering elements and building navigation bars required hacky float tricks. Vertical centering was notoriously difficult.
whyItExists.solution: Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout system. Set display: flex on a container and its children automatically align in a row (or column), distribute space, and can be centred trivially.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Navigation bars, button groups, card rows, centring content, distributing space between items — any single-axis layout.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: For two-dimensional layouts (rows AND columns simultaneously) use CSS Grid instead.

explainModes.beginner: Flexbox lines children up in a row (or column) and lets you control how they space out. You can say 'space them equally', 'push them to the right', or 'centre them vertically' — all with one or two properties.
explainModes.simple: Set display: flex on the parent. Children automatically line up in a row. justify-content distributes space along the row. align-items aligns them vertically. gap adds space between items.
explainModes.standard: The flex container controls the main axis (row/column) with flex-direction. justify-content aligns along the main axis; align-items along the cross axis. Flex items can grow (flex-grow), shrink (flex-shrink), and have a base size (flex-basis) — combined in the flex shorthand.
explainModes.technical: Flexbox resolves sizes in three steps: (1) compute hypothetical main size using flex-basis, (2) distribute free space by flex-grow/shrink ratios, (3) resolve cross-axis alignment. The flex algorithm runs after the box model. Negative free space activates flex-shrink. order changes visual order without changing DOM order — use with caution for accessibility.
explainModes.deepDive: The flex formatting context creates an independent stacking context. flex: 1 is shorthand for flex: 1 1 0 — grow freely, shrink freely, base size 0. flex: auto is 1 1 auto (base size is intrinsic). flex: none is 0 0 auto — completely rigid. When flex-wrap: wrap is set, each row forms an independent flex line and align-items applies per line. align-content (not align-items) controls spacing between wrapped lines.

content.text: Use gap instead of margins between flex items. Gap only applies between items (not to the outer edges), so you avoid the old 'first/last child margin' hack.

questions.question: Which property centres flex items along the MAIN axis?
questions.explanation: justify-content controls distribution along the main axis (horizontal by default). align-items controls alignment along the cross axis (vertical by default).

questions.question: What does flex: 1 actually mean in full?
questions.explanation: flex: 1 expands to flex: 1 1 0 — flex-grow: 1 (share available space equally), flex-shrink: 1 (can shrink), flex-basis: 0 (start from zero width).

questions.question: Flexbox is the best tool for two-dimensional (rows and columns) layouts.
questions.explanation: Flexbox is a ONE-dimensional layout tool (a single row or column). For two-dimensional layouts, use CSS Grid.

faq.q: What is the difference between justify-content and align-items?
faq.a: justify-content distributes space along the MAIN axis (horizontal in row direction). align-items aligns items along the CROSS axis (vertical in row direction). Both axes flip if flex-direction: column.

faq.q: When should I use flex: 1 vs flex: auto?
faq.a: flex: 1 (grow from 0) distributes space equally regardless of content size. flex: auto (grow from intrinsic size) starts from each item's natural width — so larger content gets proportionally more space.

faq.q: What is flex-wrap and why use it?
faq.a: By default flex items all stay on one line and may shrink to fit. flex-wrap: wrap allows items to move to a new row when they would overflow — creating a responsive card grid without media queries.
